ai.description: This slender snake reaches 150 cm. It is tan or yellowish with dark, diamond-shaped dorsal blotches and a distinctive dark "diadem" marking on the head. It features smooth scales and a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Spalerosophis diadema* is the presence of numerous small, granular scales on the top of the head, rather than large, symmetrical plates.
ai.habitat: The Diadem Snake inhabits arid to semi-arid regions, including sandy deserts, scrublands, and rocky foothills, typically ranging from sea level to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Diadem Snake is primarily diurnal and an active hunter, using its powerful body to constrict prey such as small rodents and lizards.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Spalerosophis diadema* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–15 eggs. Breeding typically occurs from spring through early summer, with eggs hatching in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Diadem Snake occurs across arid regions of Northwest India, including Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Punjab, ranging from lowlands up to 1,500 meters in elevation.
